short: The first emperor to reign entirely as a constitutional symbol, and the first to abdicate since 1817.
full:
Akihito acceded on his father's death in January 1989, opening the Heisei era. He was the first heir raised under the post-war settlement — tutored in part by an American, married in 1959 to Michiko Shōda, the first commoner to enter the imperial family, and a parent who broke with custom by raising his children himself. He defined the symbolic role largely by travelling: to Okinawa, to Iwo Jima, to Saipan and the Philippines, expressing regret for the war, and in 1992 becoming the first Japanese monarch to visit China.

His presence after disasters became the reign's signature. He and the empress knelt on the floor of evacuation centres after the 1995 Kobe earthquake, and in March 2011 he made the first televised address by an emperor to the nation, five days after the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. In a video message in August 2016 he said age was making the duties hard to sustain. The Diet passed a one-off law in June 2017, and he abdicated on 30 April 2019 — the first Japanese abdication in over two centuries.
